summary: Federal Communications Commission urges preservation of E-Rate program to ensure reliable broadband access for schools and libraries, emphasizing recurring costs and essential infrastructure for modern education.

claims.argument: Current discount matrix ensures fair access to broadband services
claims.evidence_quote: E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern education

claims.requested_action: reject narrowing of eligible equipment and services
claims.argument: Narrowing eligibility would leave students without adequate support
claims.evidence_quote: Reject proposals that would unnecessarily narrow E-Rate eligibility or restrict support based solely on geography or other criteria that would leave students without adequate support

claims.argument: E-Rate support is recurring cost for maintaining network infrastructure
claims.evidence_quote: Putnam City Independent School District 1 has received $4.79 million in committed federal E-Rate support over funding years 2021–2025 — an average of roughly $958,851 a year toward the connections our students depend on.

claims.requested_action: preserve support for special construction and dark fiber
claims.argument: Special construction and dark fiber are essential for reliable educational access
claims.evidence_quote: Preserve support for the connectivity and internal network infrastructure schools need to provide reliable educational access
